stops.note: Moneta was a title of the goddess Juno, and Rome's mint stood by her temple on the Capitoline, so her name came to mean coin (and gave English 'money' and 'mint')
'coin of gold'; after gold was struck in Brazil's Minas Gerais in the 1690s, a flood of Brazilian gold passed through Lisbon's mint
the 1703 Methuen Treaty tied English cloth to Portuguese wine, and trade surpluses drew so much Portuguese gold to Britain that moidores circulated widely, especially in Ireland

current_meaning: a former Portuguese gold coin, once current in Britain and Ireland
